newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 9.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- Two of three Northern Ireland voters believe a political settlement will not be reached at the multi-party talks which resume at Stormont on Monday.

- The Irish Prime Minister, John Bruton, will ask American President Bill Clinton on Monday to renew his forthright commitment to support an agreement reached by the Northern Ireland parties through negotiations in the multi-party talks.
- European Union foreign ministers have sent a strong signal that they expect the October 5 summit in Dublin to shift the treaty reform process up a gear.

- The release date in Ireland and the UK for the film Michael Collins will not be influenced by concerns about its possible effect on the political situation in Northern Ireland, director Neil Jordan said on Sunday.
- Saddam Hussein raised the stakes on Sunday in his power game with Washington when he sent his troops further into Kurdish territory and captured two more towns.
- Receiver Tom Grace and other key figures in the Donegal eviction controversy have put tight security measures in place following loyalist death threats.

- A new survey reveals that Irish motorists can save up to four punts on a tank of fuel by shopping around while prices can vary widely between filling stations, even between outlets on the same stretch of road.
- Ireland's 800 post-primary schools could face industrial action if a new 66.7 million Irish pound pay, promotions and pensions deal for teachers is not finalised soon.
